interpretations.explanation: Older progenitors in massive/high-σ hosts have lower C/O ratios, leading to faster-declining (lower x1) SNe Ia. This is the well-known host mass step.
Proper time flows slower in deep potentials, so SN light curves should appear stretched (higher x1) from external observer.
Standard progenitor effect (r ~ -0.5) may dominate a smaller TEP time dilation effect (r ~ +0.2). Net result is negative but less negative than pure standard physics would predict.
interpretations.testable: Compare observed slope to theoretical standard-only prediction
interpretations.interpretation: Observed slope is 28% less negative than standard prediction - could indicate partial TEP contribution

A_sn_stretch.note: SN Ia stretch clearly correlates negatively with host σ, opposite to naive TEP prediction. Standard progenitor physics provides natural explanation. TEP would need to operate as a secondary correction to the dominant standard effect.

AZ_HB_RGB.effect: HB phase strongly suppressed in inner galaxy
AZ_HB_RGB.tep_interpretation: HB phase duration affected by time dilation in deep potential
AZ_HB_RGB.standard_alternative: Metallicity gradient affects HB morphology (higher Z → redder HB)
AZ_HB_RGB.discriminator: Control for [Fe/H] - if signal persists, favors TEP

BL_WD_Mass.effect: Inner WDs appear fainter/more massive than outer WDs
BL_WD_Mass.tep_interpretation: Slower cooling in deep potential → WDs appear older/fainter
BL_WD_Mass.discriminator: Control for extinction and formation epoch

BC_YSO.effect: YSOs in dense regions appear younger/puffier
BC_YSO.tep_interpretation: Contraction timescale stretched by time dilation
BC_YSO.discriminator: Compare YSO properties at fixed environment density

AG_Distance.effect: Inner galaxy stars appear fainter than geometric distance predicts
AG_Distance.tep_interpretation: TEP fading effect in deep potential

BX_Binary.effect: Deficit of close binaries in inner galaxy
BX_Binary.tep_interpretation: Orbital decay timescale stretched → binaries survive longer as wide
BX_Binary.discriminator: Binary period distribution vs potential depth

B_strong_signals.overall_assessment: Five strong correlations show TEP-predicted signs, but all have viable standard physics alternatives. Discriminating tests require additional controls (metallicity, extinction, selection).

C_qso_feii.note: True FeII clock test requires FeII EW measurements from specialized pipeline (e.g., Shen et al. SDSS QSO catalog). Standard specLine table does not include FeII.

BZ_Carbon.anomaly: C/M ratio peaks in inner galaxy, opposite to metallicity gradient
BZ_Carbon.standard_expectation: C-stars form preferentially at low metallicity → outer galaxy
possible_explanations: TEP: AGB thermal pulse timescales affected by potential → more C dredge-up in deep potential
Standard: Binary mass transfer more efficient in dense environments
Selection: C-star detection efficiency varies with extinction
BZ_Carbon.discriminator: Compare C/N ratio which should not show same pattern under standard model

BW_CEMP.anomaly: Flat or negative CEMP gradient, missing expected outer enhancement
BW_CEMP.standard_expectation: CEMP-s/r stars trace early enrichment → outer halo dominated
possible_explanations: TEP: Binary evolution timescales (mass transfer) affected uniformly
Standard: CEMP-no class (non-binary) dominates → no spatial gradient expected
Selection: CEMP detection harder at low S/N in outer halo

BS_Msigma.anomaly: M-σ steepens at high mass instead of flattening
BS_Msigma.standard_expectation: BH growth saturates as feedback becomes efficient
possible_explanations: TEP: BH accretion timescales stretched in deep potentials → larger BHs
Standard: Dry mergers add BH mass without σ growth at high mass
Selection: High-mass BHs easier to detect → Malmquist bias

D_anomalies.overall_assessment: Three anomalies show patterns opposite to standard predictions. These could indicate new physics (TEP?) or unmodeled systematics.
